name: Google OAuth Web Credentials Automation

mission.primary_objective: Give Ringdom engineers a single authoritative reference for automating everything around 'Sign in with Google' for first-party web apps (Auth.js / NextAuth v4+), centered on the OAuth 2.0 Web Application client created under Google Auth Platform → Clients, whose client IDs end in .apps.googleusercontent.com.
mission.context: As of 2026 Google has rebranded and moved the OAuth consent screen and credentials pages from APIs & Services to a dedicated navigation section called Google Auth Platform. The artifact of interest is the Web application OAuth client type. No fully-supported, GA REST API or gcloud command exists for creating this credential type as of April 2026. The only supported programmatic alternatives involve workarounds, Firebase/Identity Platform delegation, or accepting a manual creation step with automated secret rotation afterward.
mission.target_outcome: Engineers understand exactly which automation is officially supported, what is a workaround, why google_iam_oauth_client and google_iap_client are the wrong tools, and what operational playbooks exist for each situation.
mission.scope: Google Auth Platform Web OAuth clients (.apps.googleusercontent.com), consent screen configuration, Auth.js v5 / NextAuth v4+ GoogleProvider integration, Terraform hashicorp/google provider, gcloud CLI iam oauth-clients group, Firebase / Identity Platform as alternatives, Secret Manager rotation.

truth_lens: Creating a Web application OAuth client (.apps.googleusercontent.com) under Google Auth Platform has no supported GA REST API or gcloud command as of April 2026 — manual console creation is the only officially supported path. The google_iap_client Terraform resource is permanently defunct (March 2026), and google_iam_oauth_client manages Workforce Identity Federation clients with UUID-format IDs that are incompatible with Auth.js GoogleProvider and GIS One Tap. The recommended operational strategy is: create the client once manually, immediately store the GOCSPX- secret in Secret Manager, and automate everything downstream (secret rotation, env injection, consent screen scope updates via console). Firebase / Identity Platform offers a programmatic IdP-config API as an alternative architecture if the team is open to that dependency.
consult_when: setting up or automating Sign in with Google for a web application using Auth.js or NextAuth
deciding which Terraform resource to use for Google OAuth client management
evaluating whether google_iam_oauth_client or google_iap_client are appropriate for your use case
designing the secret management strategy for GOCSPX- credentials
troubleshooting redirect_uri_mismatch, invalid_client, or refresh token issues
evaluating Firebase Auth / Identity Platform as an alternative to direct OAuth client management
understanding the OAuth consent screen lifecycle (Testing vs Production, verification requirements)
planning for OAuth client secret rotation without downtime
evaluating risk of browser automation for console-based credential creation
key_patterns: Pattern: map requirement -> consult_when hit for google_oauth_web_credentials_automation -> apply truth_lens constraints before code.
Pattern: validate external API/env assumptions against this lens before merge or deploy.
expertise: Google OAuth Web Credentials Automation: domain execution patterns per lens body.
role: LegioX truth lens — Google OAuth Web Credentials Automation
core_expertise: Give Ringdom engineers a single authoritative reference for automating everything around 'Sign in with Google' for first-party web apps (Auth.js / NextAuth v4+), centered on the OAuth 2.0 Web Application client created under Google Auth Platform → Clients, whose client IDs end in .apps.googleusercontent.com.
core_principles: NO_GA_API_FOR_WEB_CLIENT — As of April 2026, no documented GA REST API or gcloud command can create a Web application OAuth client (type=WEB) under Google Auth Platform / APIs & Services Credentials. Manual creation via console is required for the initial provisioning step.

WRONG_TOOL_WARNING — google_iap_client (deprecated March 2026) and google_iam_oauth_client both produce different credential types and client ID formats from .apps.googleusercontent.com web clients; they are NOT interchangeable for Auth.js GoogleProvider.

SECRET_VISIBLE_ONCE — As of June 2025, Google masks OAuth client secrets after creation; the GOCSPX- prefixed secret must be downloaded immediately and stored in Secret Manager or equivalent; it cannot be retrieved later from the console.
INACTIVE_CLIENT_DELETION — OAuth clients unused for six months are automatically deleted by Google; ensure the client is used in OAuth/token flows or update its configuration within that window.

CONSENT_SCREEN_PREREQUISITE — A configured OAuth consent screen (now called the Google Auth Platform branding/overview page) is required before any client can be created; external user type apps in Testing mode issue 7-day refresh tokens unless only openid/email/profile scopes are requested.

AUTH_JS_REQUIRES_WEB_CLIENT — Auth.js GoogleProvider uses the authorization code flow with PKCE-optional server-side callback to /api/auth/callback/google; it requires a Web application client with that redirect URI registered; no other client type satisfies this requirement without code changes.
ROTATE_DO_NOT_RECREATE — Prefer secret rotation (add new secret, migrate, delete old) over deleting and recreating clients; client ID changes break all deployed environment variables.

credential_taxonomy.overview: Four distinct credential types exist in Google's ecosystem; engineers frequently confuse them. Only type (1) supports Auth.js GoogleProvider for end-user Sign in with Google.

1_web_application_oauth_client.console_path: Google Auth Platform → Clients → Create Client → Application type: Web application
1_web_application_oauth_client.legacy_path: APIs & Services → Credentials → OAuth client ID (still redirects as of 2026)

required_fields.authorized_javascript_origins: Origin of the frontend (e.g. https://ring.example.com); needed for GIS One Tap
required_fields.authorized_redirect_uris: Must include the Auth.js callback URI exactly: https://{domain}/api/auth/callback/google

authjs_compat.notes: Direct match. Set AUTH_GOOGLE_ID and AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET (Auth.js v5) or GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET (NextAuth v4). Redirect URI must be registered exactly. For refresh tokens, pass access_type=offline and prompt=consent in authorization params.

gis_one_tap_compat.notes: The NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID env var must be this same .apps.googleusercontent.com ID. Authorized JavaScript origins must include the page origin.

2_iam_oauth_client.console_path: IAM & Admin → Workforce Identity → OAuth clients
2_iam_oauth_client.purpose: Used exclusively for Workforce Identity Federation — letting enterprise workforce users access Google Cloud resources. Requires a workforce identity pool and provider.

authjs_compat.notes: INCOMPATIBLE. The UUID-format client ID and the audience/issuer expectations of this client type are not accepted by Google's consumer OAuth endpoints used by Auth.js. Do not attempt to use this for Sign in with Google on consumer web apps.

gis_one_tap_compat.notes: GIS One Tap requires .apps.googleusercontent.com format client IDs explicitly.

3_iap_client_deprecated.deprecation_status: DEPRECATED — Jan 22, 2025; IAP OAuth Admin API permanently shut down March 19, 2026
3_iap_client_deprecated.purpose: Was used to create OAuth clients scoped to IAP-protected resources (internal org only via API; external required manual Console creation). IAP now uses Google-managed OAuth clients by default.

authjs_compat.notes: INCOMPATIBLE and DEFUNCT. API is shut down. This was never the right type for Auth.js GoogleProvider regardless.

4_service_account_key.client_id_format: Numeric unique_id field in JSON, email: name@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
4_service_account_key.purpose: Machine-to-machine server authentication. Does NOT represent a human user.

authjs_compat.notes: INCOMPATIBLE for user-facing Sign in with Google. Service accounts cannot consent on behalf of human users.

confusion_matrix.common_mistake_1: Using google_iam_oauth_client and expecting .apps.googleusercontent.com format — will fail silently or with invalid_client.
confusion_matrix.common_mistake_2: Using google_iap_client for non-IAP web login — wrong product, wrong flow, now defunct.
confusion_matrix.common_mistake_3: Assuming gcloud iam oauth-clients maps to Google Auth Platform web clients — it does not; it manages Workforce Identity Federation clients only.

target_outcome_contract.definition_of_success: Automation is considered SUCCESS only when ALL of the following conditions hold:
checklist: User can complete Google OAuth login on the production domain (and staging domain if applicable) via Auth.js /api/auth/signin route
The id_token audience (aud claim) returned by Google matches the .apps.googleusercontent.com client ID configured in AUTH_GOOGLE_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
The redirect_uri used by Auth.js (/api/auth/callback/google) is registered as an Authorized redirect URI on the Web application client
The authorized_javascript_origins includes the production origin for GIS One Tap to function
For refresh token support: authorization params include access_type=offline and prompt=consent; a database adapter is configured or JWT callback handles token storage
The GOCSPX- client secret is stored in Secret Manager (or equivalent) and injected via environment variables at runtime — never committed to git
The OAuth consent screen (Google Auth Platform branding) is configured with: app name, support email, authorized domains matching the production domain, and privacy policy / TOS URLs
App publishing status is set to 'In production' for non-Google-Workspace apps with public users, OR test users are explicitly added while status is 'Testing'
Scopes declared on the consent screen match what Auth.js requests (minimum: openid, email, profile)
An inactive-client monitoring process or cron exists to prevent auto-deletion (6-month inactivity rule)
Secret rotation runbook is documented and tested

oauth_consent_screen.location: Google Auth Platform → Overview → Get Started (or existing branding configuration)
oauth_consent_screen.user_type: External for public Sign in with Google; Internal if restricted to org Google Workspace
oauth_consent_screen.scopes: openid, email, profile are non-sensitive and require no verification; any additional Google API scopes may require OAuth app verification
oauth_consent_screen.testing_mode_limit: In Testing status, refresh tokens expire in 7 days unless only openid/email/profile requested; limited to 100 test users
oauth_consent_screen.production_status: Required for public apps; sensitive/restricted scopes require Google verification (can take weeks)

official_automation_inventory.research_note: Searched Google Cloud documentation, Google Developers Blog (April 2025 Google Auth Platform announcement), Terraform Registry, gcloud CLI docs, and open GitHub issues. No GA REST API for creating Web application OAuth clients was found as of this date.

1_rest_api_web_oauth_client.description: A public REST API to create/manage Web application OAuth clients under Google Auth Platform
1_rest_api_web_oauth_client.supports_web_oauth_client_type_1: NO — not documented, not discoverable via $discovery endpoint as of April 2026
1_rest_api_web_oauth_client.stability: N/A — does not exist as a public GA API
1_rest_api_web_oauth_client.evidence: GitHub issue hashicorp/terraform-provider-google#1287 (2018) noted 'I can't actually find any API for managing OAuth 2.0 credentials.' Issue #6074 (2020) and #16452 (2023) confirmed the same gap. No Google documentation page exists for a REST API to create APIs & Services / Google Auth Platform web clients. The IAP OAuth Admin API that partially overlapped was deprecated Jan 2025 and shut down March 2026.

2_gcloud_iam_oauth_clients.description: gcloud iam oauth-clients create / describe / list / delete
2_gcloud_iam_oauth_clients.supports_web_oauth_client_type_1: NO — manages Workforce Identity Federation OAuth clients (UUID format IDs), NOT Google Auth Platform web clients (.apps.googleusercontent.com)
2_gcloud_iam_oauth_clients.warning: Naming is maximally confusing. Despite the command group being called 'iam oauth-clients', it does not touch the credentials shown at console.cloud.google.com/auth/clients.

3_terraform_google_iap_client.supports_web_oauth_client_type_1: NO — creates IAP-scoped internal-org OAuth clients only; also now permanently defunct
3_terraform_google_iap_client.stability: DEPRECATED — deprecated Jan 22, 2025; non-functional after March 19, 2026
3_terraform_google_iap_client.warning: Do not use. The underlying IAP OAuth Admin API is permanently shut down. New projects cannot use these APIs. Even before shutdown, created clients were locked to IAP usage and could not have redirect URIs updated.

4_terraform_google_iam_oauth_client.supports_web_oauth_client_type_1: NO — Workforce Identity Federation only; produces UUID-format client IDs incompatible with Auth.js GoogleProvider
4_terraform_google_iam_oauth_client.stability: GA (for its intended Workforce Identity use case)
4_terraform_google_iam_oauth_client.known_issues: Issue #22530: allowed_redirect_uris requires the generated client_id in the URI, creating a chicken-and-egg problem requiring a POST then PATCH workaround.

5_terraform_google_iap_client_programmat.description: identityAwareProxyClients.create REST API (IAP OAuth Admin API)
5_terraform_google_iap_client_programmat.supports_web_oauth_client_type_1: NO — was limited to internal-org IAP clients; permanently shut down March 19, 2026

6_firebase_identity_toolkit_api.description: Google Cloud Identity Platform REST API (identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/v2) — configures IdP settings within Firebase/Identity Platform projects
6_firebase_identity_toolkit_api.supports_web_oauth_client_type_1: PARTIAL — can configure which Google client ID/secret a Firebase project uses for Google sign-in, but does NOT create the underlying .apps.googleusercontent.com client itself; the client must already exist

7_google_auth_platform_ui.description: Manual creation via Google Cloud Console → Google Auth Platform → Clients
7_google_auth_platform_ui.supports_web_oauth_client_type_1: YES — the only fully supported method as of April 2026
7_google_auth_platform_ui.notes: As of April 2025, the consent screen and credentials pages have a dedicated navigation section 'Google Auth Platform' replacing the old APIs & Services location. Client secrets are shown only once at creation and must be downloaded immediately.

gap_analysis_and_feature_requests.summary: The inability to programmatically create Web application OAuth clients (.apps.googleusercontent.com type) is a longstanding gap, with open GitHub issues spanning 2018–2024 and no resolution confirmed as of April 2026.

key_issues.title: Resource to create OAuth 2.0 credentials
key_issues.insight: Original issue acknowledged 'I can't actually find any API for managing OAuth 2.0 credentials' — the gap is at the Google API level, not the Terraform level.

key_issues.title: Creating OAuth 2.0 Client IDs (from GCP console) using this provider
key_issues.insight: Explicit request for Web application type. No resolution.

key_issues.title: Create OAuth 2.0 Client ID (non-IAP) resource
key_issues.proposed_resource: google_oauth_client with application_type='Web application', authorized_javascript_origins, authorized_redirect_uris
key_issues.insight: A Terraform resource was proposed but not yet merged or released as of April 2026. The label 'forward/review' suggests active consideration but no GA availability.

gap_analysis_and_feature_requests.roadmap_inference: If/when Google releases a public API for creating web OAuth clients, the Terraform resource google_oauth_client (issue #16452) would likely be the implementation vehicle. Monitor the hashicorp/terraform-provider-google changelog and Google Auth Platform release notes.
gap_analysis_and_feature_requests.do_not_use_undocumented_endpoints: Several internal console.cloud.google.com endpoints exist that proxy OAuth client creation. These are NOT public APIs, have no stability guarantee, no IAM permission model, no audit logging via Cloud Audit Logs, and their use likely violates Google Cloud Terms of Service. Do not build automation against them.
gap_analysis_and_feature_requests.iap_deprecation_impact: The March 2026 shutdown of the IAP OAuth Admin API removes the only previously-available programmatic path for creating any IAP-scoped OAuth client. Teams relying on google_iap_brand and google_iap_client in Terraform must migrate to Google-managed OAuth clients for IAP or use pre-created custom clients.

recommended_automation_playbooks.ranking_note: Playbooks are ranked from most to least preferred. Read the Playbook description fully before choosing.

playbook_A.title: Official API path (future-state)
playbook_A.precondition: A GA REST API or gcloud command for creating Web application OAuth clients has been released
playbook_A.trigger: Monitor https://cloud.google.com/release-notes and hashicorp/terraform-provider-google changelog for google_oauth_client resource release
steps: When available: use google_oauth_client Terraform resource or REST API with application_type=WEB
Store client_id as a non-secret Terraform output or env variable
Capture client_secret IMMEDIATELY from API response — store to Secret Manager in the same automation step
Configure authorized_redirect_uris: include /api/auth/callback/google for each environment
Configure authorized_javascript_origins: include the frontend origin for GIS One Tap
Set AUTH_GOOGLE_ID and AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET in your deployment environment from Secret Manager
playbook_A.iam_permissions_needed: Unknown — will depend on released API; expect something like oauth.clients.create or cloudauth.clients.create at project level
playbook_A.status: NOT YET AVAILABLE as of April 2026 — do not plan against this until a GA release is confirmed

playbook_B.title: IAM OAuth client path (Workforce Identity) — why it fails Auth.js
playbook_B.warning: DO NOT USE for Auth.js GoogleProvider / Sign in with Google. This playbook documents why, not how.
playbook_B.what_google_iam_oauth_client_creates: A Workforce Identity Federation OAuth client with a UUID-format client_id (not .apps.googleusercontent.com). The token issuer, audience, and discovery document are scoped to your Workforce Identity pool, not to Google's consumer OAuth endpoints.
why_it_fails_authjs: Auth.js GoogleProvider uses https://accounts.google.com as the issuer and expects .apps.googleusercontent.com client IDs in the aud claim of returned ID tokens
Workforce Identity clients authenticate against https://iam.googleapis.com/v1/locations/global/workforcePools/... endpoints, not https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth
The redirect_uri for Auth.js (/api/auth/callback/google) will not be accepted by Workforce Identity token flows
GIS One Tap explicitly requires .apps.googleusercontent.com format client IDs
playbook_B.valid_use_case: Workforce Identity Federation OAuth clients are the right tool when employees or partners authenticate to Google Cloud CLI / APIs using an external corporate IdP. They are not a Sign in with Google mechanism for end users of your web app.

playbook_C.title: IaC + Secret Manager + rotation (after manual client creation)
playbook_C.precondition: Web application OAuth client has been created manually in Google Auth Platform console; client_id and initial client_secret are known
playbook_C.recommended_for: Production environments where the client was created once and needs automated secret rotation and config injection
steps: Store initial client_secret in Secret Manager: gcloud secrets create google-oauth-client-secret --data-file=<(echo -n 'GOCSPX-...')
Grant the app's service account roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor on the specific secret
In your deployment pipeline (Cloud Run, GKE, etc.), mount the secret as an environment variable: AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET via Secret Manager integration
Store client_id as a non-secret environment variable (it is public-safe): AUTH_GOOGLE_ID=<number>.apps.googleusercontent.com
For Terraform: manage authorized_redirect_uris updates via a null_resource + gcloud workaround (see note below) or accept manual console updates for URI changes

Secret rotation procedure: in Google Auth Platform console, click 'Add secret' on the client → download new secret → update Secret Manager secret version → deploy new version → verify auth flows → disable old secret → delete old secret after 24h grace period
Automate rotation reminder: set a Cloud Scheduler job to alert 30 days before 6-month inactivity threshold if client has no token activity

what_you_can_manage_in_tf: google_secret_manager_secret + google_secret_manager_secret_version — store and rotate the secret
google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member — grant access to app SA
google_cloud_run_v2_service — inject AUTH_GOOGLE_ID as env var, AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET from secret ref
null_resource with local-exec — placeholder to document the manual client creation step
terraform_partial_automation.what_cannot_be_managed_in_tf: The OAuth client itself (client type, redirect URIs, JavaScript origins) — manual console step

playbook_C.note_on_redirect_uri_updates: When adding new environments (new staging domain, etc.), authorized_redirect_uris must be updated manually in Google Auth Platform or via whatever API becomes available. Document this as a runbook step.

playbook_D.title: UI automation last resort (browser automation against console.cloud.google.com)
playbook_D.warning: HIGH RISK. Read threat model before considering this path. This should be a last resort only, used once for bootstrapping, never as routine automation.
playbook_D.when_to_consider: When there is genuine organizational need to script the first-time provisioning of many projects at scale and manual steps are operationally impossible
threat_model: Session hijack: browser automation sessions with GCP console credentials are extremely high-value targets; if the automation host is compromised, an attacker gains console-level access
Brittle selectors: Google Auth Platform UI is being actively redesigned (migrated from APIs & Services in 2025); selectors will break without warning
ToS risk: Google's Terms of Service prohibit automated access to its services except through documented APIs; verify your organization's legal position and org policy before proceeding
No audit trail: actions taken via console automation do not produce the same Cloud Audit Log entries as API calls; security teams may flag this
Secret exfiltration risk: the GOCSPX- secret appears only once in the UI; automation must capture it immediately and route it only to approved secret stores
minimum_safeguards_if_used: Run on an isolated, dedicated automation host with no other credentials mounted
Use a dedicated GCP admin service account with only the permissions needed, not a human account
Capture client_secret IMMEDIATELY and write only to Secret Manager — never to disk, logs, or stdout
Implement break-glass manual procedure: a human can always override and rotate the secret if automation fails mid-run
Scope use to one-time bootstrap only; do not make this part of a regular pipeline
Log the initiation and completion of the automation run to Cloud Logging with a custom log entry, even if the internal steps are not logged by Google
playbook_D.tos_advisory: The authors recommend verifying with your legal/compliance team that browser automation against console.cloud.google.com does not violate your Google Cloud agreement or acceptable use policy before implementing this approach.

playbook_E.title: Firebase Auth / Identity Platform as product alternative
playbook_E.when_to_consider: When the team prefers a managed authentication layer over direct OAuth client management, especially for multi-provider auth, user management, and token abstraction

what_changes: Auth.js GoogleProvider is replaced by Firebase Auth SDK (or remains as a wrapper if using firebase-auth adapter)
User sessions are backed by Firebase ID tokens, not Google OAuth tokens directly
The .apps.googleusercontent.com client ID still exists, but is managed within the Firebase project's Authentication settings
Client ID and secret are configured in Firebase Console → Authentication → Sign-in method → Google, OR via identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/v2 REST API
what_you_gain: Programmatic IdP configuration via identitytoolkit REST API (documented, GA)
Built-in user database, email verification, password reset
Terraform resource google_identity_platform_default_supported_idp_config for IdP config management
Admin SDK for server-side user management
what_you_lose: Direct control over the OAuth flow — Firebase proxies it
Auth.js-native session management (must use firebase-auth adapter or custom session logic)
Simpler token audience model — ID tokens are now issued by Firebase, not Google accounts directly
Potentially: simpler deployment topology (Firebase adds a dependency)
architecture_change.terraform_resource: google_identity_platform_default_supported_idp_config (manages which Google client ID/secret the Firebase project uses for google.com IdP)
architecture_change.important_caveat: Even with Firebase Auth, the underlying .apps.googleusercontent.com client must exist and be configured; Firebase does not create it. Firebase's automation advantage is in the IdP config step, not the client creation step.
architecture_change.recommendation: If Ringdom's Ring Platform already uses Firebase or is open to it for the auth layer, Identity Platform is a well-supported path with real programmatic management APIs. If the stack is Auth.js + Next.js without Firebase, the operational cost is lower to stay on direct OAuth with Playbook C.

auth_js_integration_reference.version_note: Covers Auth.js v5 (package: next-auth v5 beta / @auth/*) and NextAuth v4

provider_config.minimal: Google() from next-auth/providers/google — client ID/secret auto-read from env vars
provider_config.with_refresh_tokens: Google({ authorization: { params: { access_type: 'offline', prompt: 'consent' } } }) — forces refresh token issuance; Google only provides refresh token on first consent unless prompt=consent is set
provider_config.refresh_token_note: Google issues refresh tokens only on first authorization per user per client. To force re-issuance: pass prompt=consent, or instruct user to revoke at https://myaccount.google.com/permissions
provider_config.id_token_audience_check: The aud claim in the returned ID token will be the .apps.googleusercontent.com client ID; Auth.js verifies this automatically

gis_one_tap_compatibility.requires: Same .apps.googleusercontent.com client ID used in GoogleProvider; authorized_javascript_origins must include the page's origin
gis_one_tap_compatibility.env_var: NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID — must be set for client-side GIS script
gis_one_tap_compatibility.consent_screen_requirement: App must be in production status OR the user must be a registered test user for One Tap to function
gis_one_tap_compatibility.note: GIS One Tap and Auth.js can share the same client ID; the GIS credential callback can feed into NextAuth.js signIn() call

common_errors.redirect_uri_mismatch: The redirect_uri in the authorization request does not match any registered URI. Fix: add https://{domain}/api/auth/callback/google to Authorized redirect URIs in Google Auth Platform console.
common_errors.invalid_client: Client ID or secret is wrong, or the client was deleted. Verify AUTH_GOOGLE_ID/AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET. Check for inactive-client auto-deletion.
common_errors.access_denied: User denied consent, or app is in Testing status and user is not a registered test user.
common_errors.refresh_token_missing: access_type=offline was not set, or user has already authorized the app (refresh token only on first authorization). Use prompt=consent to force re-consent.
common_errors.token_7_day_expiry: App is in Testing status with non-profile scopes; refresh tokens expire in 7 days. Publish the app or request verification.
common_errors.unverified_app_warning: App uses sensitive/restricted scopes without Google verification; users see a warning screen. Reduce scopes or complete verification.

for_secret_manager: roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor — app service account reading the secret at runtime
roles/secretmanager.secretVersionManager — rotation automation service account adding/destroying secret versions
automation_principal_least_privilege.for_project_provisioning: See google-cloud-console-agent.json for full project provisioning IAM model
automation_principal_least_privilege.for_firebase_idp_config: roles/firebaseauth.admin or roles/editor on the Firebase project (latter is too broad; prefer fine-grained Firebase Admin SDK)

secret_storage_rules: Never commit GOCSPX- secrets to git, even in private repos or encrypted secrets files without proper key management
Store in Secret Manager; mount as env var in Cloud Run / GKE via Secret Manager integration
For local dev: use .env.local (gitignored) populated from Secret Manager via gcloud secrets versions access
For CI/CD: use Secret Manager + Workload Identity Federation to inject secrets without long-lived keys
SOPS + KMS is acceptable for teams using GitOps for configuration management
External Secrets Operator (ESO) is acceptable for Kubernetes-native secret injection

org_policy_considerations.oauth_client_creation_restriction: No standard org policy constraint exists for blocking Web OAuth client creation (unlike service account keys); this is managed by IAM roles on the project
org_policy_considerations.who_can_create: Any user with Editor or Owner on the project, or with the OAuth configuration access role (if/when a fine-grained role becomes available); check with your org admin
org_policy_considerations.key_creation_block: The constraint iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation does NOT affect OAuth client secrets — different credential type
org_policy_considerations.detecting_restrictions: If users get PERMISSION_DENIED on Google Auth Platform, it may be a custom org policy; contact your GCP org admin

consent_screen_compliance.testing_vs_production: Testing: up to 100 test users; refresh tokens expire in 7 days for non-profile scopes. Production: publicly accessible; must pass verification for sensitive/restricted scopes.
consent_screen_compliance.verification_timeline: Google OAuth app verification can take days to weeks for sensitive scopes; plan accordingly for launch timelines
consent_screen_compliance.external_vs_internal: Internal (Google Workspace org only) consent screens do not require verification and are suitable for internal tools; External is required for public-facing Sign in with Google
consent_screen_compliance.domain_verification: Adding authorized domains to the consent screen may require verifying domain ownership via Google Search Console
consent_screen_compliance.branding_requirements: App name must not impersonate Google or other brands; logo must meet Google's brand guidelines; failure results in verification rejection

cloud_logging.note: Google's authorization server (accounts.google.com) does NOT write logs to your GCP project's Cloud Logging. OAuth authorization errors are not visible there.
cloud_logging.what_is_logged: Your application's server logs (Cloud Run, GKE) will show the error response from Google's token endpoint; log these explicitly in Auth.js callbacks

where_to_find_oauth_errors.auth_js_error_callbacks: Implement the error callback in Auth.js to capture and log OAuthCallbackError, OAuthSignInError, etc. to your observability stack
where_to_find_oauth_errors.google_auth_platform_console: Google Auth Platform → Clients → click client → shows last active date and basic usage indicators; not a full error log
where_to_find_oauth_errors.google_workspace_admin: For Workspace-managed accounts, some OAuth grant events appear in Workspace Admin → Reports → Audit → Token

redirect_uri_mismatch.cause: The redirect_uri parameter in the auth request does not exactly match a registered URI; case-sensitive, scheme-sensitive, path-sensitive
redirect_uri_mismatch.fix: Add the exact URI to Authorized redirect URIs in Google Auth Platform; common gotcha: http vs https, trailing slash, port number

causes: Wrong client ID or secret in environment variables
Client was deleted (manual or auto-deletion after 6 months inactivity)
Client secret was rotated and old secret is still deployed
invalid_client.fix: Verify AUTH_GOOGLE_ID and AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET; check if client exists in Google Auth Platform console; redeploy with current secret

symptoms: App shows 'unverified app' warning to users
Access denied for users outside test users list
consent_screen_misconfiguration.fix: Check app publishing status in Google Auth Platform; add test users if in Testing mode; submit for verification if using sensitive scopes

refresh_token_invalid_grant.error: invalid_grant with error_description containing 'Token has been expired or revoked'
causes: User revoked app access at https://myaccount.google.com/permissions
Google rotated the refresh token (rare, policy-based)
App was in Testing mode and 7-day TTL expired
Google Workspace session control policy expired the session
refresh_token_invalid_grant.fix: Re-initiate the OAuth flow with prompt=consent to force re-authorization

inactive_client_deleted.symptoms: invalid_client error appears unexpectedly after a period of no usage
inactive_client_deleted.cause: Google auto-deleted the OAuth client after 6 months of inactivity (no auth/token requests and no settings modifications)
inactive_client_deleted.fix: Recreate the client manually; update all environment variables with new client ID and secret; consider adding a scheduled auth request or settings update to keep the client active
inactive_client_deleted.prevention: Monitor client last-active date; set a reminder at 5 months

anti_patterns.pattern: Using google_iam_oauth_client and expecting .apps.googleusercontent.com format client ID
anti_patterns.consequence: Auth.js will fail with invalid_client; GIS One Tap will refuse to initialize; the UUID-format client ID will not be accepted by Google's consumer OAuth endpoints

anti_patterns.pattern: Storing GOCSPX- client secret in a public or private git repository
anti_patterns.consequence: Secret exposure; potential account takeover; Google may auto-revoke compromised secrets if detected via secret scanning integrations

anti_patterns.pattern: Using google_iap_client or google_iap_brand Terraform resources (deprecated)
anti_patterns.consequence: Terraform apply will fail as of March 19, 2026; the underlying API is permanently shut down

anti_patterns.pattern: Creating separate OAuth clients for each environment (dev/staging/prod) instead of one client with multiple redirect URIs
anti_patterns.consequence: Secret management complexity multiplied; higher risk of client auto-deletion if dev/staging clients are inactive

anti_patterns.pattern: Leaving app in Testing status for production deployments
anti_patterns.consequence: Refresh tokens expire in 7 days for most scopes; users get logged out; external users cannot sign in at all unless they are registered test users

anti_patterns.pattern: Relying on the IAP client type for Sign in with Google on a public web app
anti_patterns.consequence: Wrong product entirely; IAP is for protecting GCP infrastructure resources, not for implementing user authentication in your application

anti_patterns.pattern: Building browser automation against console.cloud.google.com endpoints without understanding the ToS implications
anti_patterns.consequence: Potential ToS violation; brittle automation that breaks silently; no audit trail; security risk if automation credentials are compromised

anti_patterns.pattern: Not handling the GIS One Tap / Auth.js token handoff correctly (different audiences)
anti_patterns.consequence: Security vulnerability: ID token from One Tap must be verified server-side with google-auth-library before being trusted; never trust client-side assertion alone
